_r5_statement_form.defect: R5's `setRefClass("Name", ...)` registers the generator under the DECLARED name whether or not the call is assigned to a variable, and the corpus writes it BARE at file level. Only the assignment-RHS spelling was recognised, so every statement-form class, its `fields=`/`methods=` members and its `contains=` relation were invisible. Measured over the whole admitted population (2184 files): 3 statement-form classes with a literal name — `C++Field`, `C++OverloadedMethods`, `C++Constructor`, all in `r-Rcpp/R/00_classes.R:27,37,58` — and 2 assignment-form sites.
_r5_statement_form.fix: a statement-form branch in the call handler, with three guards: it must NOT be an assignment value (the assignment path owns that spelling, or every assigned class would double-publish — the first version of this fix DID, because tree-sitter hands out a fresh JS wrapper per node access and an `===` guard silently failed; the guard uses the analyzer's `sameNode` index comparison), it must be FILE-LEVEL (`fnStack.length === 0`, the same rule the assignment path applies to locals), and the class NAME must be a literal string — `setRefClass(Class, ...)` computes its name at runtime and has no publishable identity.
_r5_statement_form.measured: whole-population gate `r 0`: contains 17,629 -> 17,651 edges (+22 = 3 class symbols' `contains global -> Name` rows + 19 member rows), extends 145 and mixes_in 206 UNCHANGED, TOTAL 80,101 -> 80,123. 2184/2184 admitted, 0 excluded. Artifact: validation/m14/fixtures/r/measurements/r-gate-r5statement.txt.

mixes_in.rung: R3 — expressed on node types the pinned build already has (`call`, `argument`, `string`, `identifier`); NO grammar change. The construct is a call argument, so the ladder's R1/R2 rungs are not needed and not claimed.
mixes_in.construct: R's composition clause `contains=` on BOTH class spellings — `setClass` (S4) and `setRefClass` (R5) — when the clause is LIST-SHAPED (`contains = c("A", "B")`, two or more entries). Source = the composing class, target = each composed class's SYMBOL (bare name; a `pkg::Class` qualifier is dropped, because a symbol spelled `pkg::Class` binds to nothing). No `partRole`: that key is mandatory on `part_of` rows only, and a wrong marker is worse than a missing one. Emitted with `relationshipSubType` `s4_composes`/`r5_composes`.
mixes_in.why_the_split: The one-class shape is a SUPERtype and stays `extends`: R's own `is()`/`extends()` answer TRUE for a single named `contains=`, and R6's `inherit=` and S7's `parent=` are single-base conformance too. Relabelling those would publish a false edge. What makes the LIST shape `mixes_in` is the fleet's own definition (`src/ast/types.ts:156-160`: 'no single base and the `with` list is not an inheritance clause') and the Scala `extends A with B, C` precedent that labels the later positions `mixes_in`.
mixes_in.caveat: STATED, NOT HIDDEN: R's `contains=` also makes `is()` TRUE for the composed classes, so the list-shape label is the fleet's composition-clause reading, NOT a claim that no conformance exists. A single-base clause is never relabelled.
